title: An L^3 bound for the trilinear Hilbert transform
main_claim: The trilinear Hilbert transform with slopes 1,2,3 maps L^3×L^3×L^3 to L^1. The paper reduces this to a uniform sparse-type bound Σ|I||H_I| ≤ C_N ∫∏M_q f_j with q slightly above 2. That bound is proved by absorption, C_N ≤ CA + cC_N, which needs a long construction: the Leng–Sah–Sawhney U^3 inverse theorem, compression of projections, curvature localization, side and short-block estimates, and counting of the core terms.
coverage:
Checked in detail:
(1) outer.tex: the local absolute estimate; the preliminary bound C_N ≲ N; the stopping-time removal of normalization (stops cover at most |J|/4, the E_J sets, and C_N ≤ CA + CcC_N); and the recovery of the continuous kernel. That includes the vanishing marginals of W = ∏(∂_S − j∂_X)[ωφ], the identity Σ_m W = φ^{(4)}, the integral ∫φ^{(4)}(t/a)da/a^2 = −φ^{(3)}(0)/t, and the rescaling a^{-1}W = r^{-1}w_I.
(2) charts.tex: the continuous inverse lemma. This covers the cube bounds, the discretization with no wraparound, the step-2 group law and conversion of the nilsequence into atoms, and the exact floor-interpolation phase identity. I verified that identity symbolically with sympy for a general non-symmetric C.
(3) sides.tex: the mixed-norm maximal lemma via extrapolation, and the whole short-block comparison (Lemma 16). This covers the slow-lattice/fast-torus lift; the quadratic randomization invariance (Σ m_j^2/c_j = 0 on the progression nullspace, with c = (−1,3,−3,1)); the fourth-moment bound; the regular-slot bound e_j ≤ C; the clipping; the reconstruction from bursts; the exponent bookkeeping (Σ1/p_j = 1, fast exponents with sum at most 2, p_* = 2q − 2 > q); and the final power (K+2)^{11(q−2)/(q−1)}. I also checked the near-band sparse estimate that gives P^{-1/2}.
(4) localization.tex: the algebraic transfer identity (15), i.e. band weights (P − p + 1)/P giving coefficient (p − q)/P.
(5) compression.tex: the coefficient and projection bounds, the binary-prefix lemma, and the bound S ≤ C log(2D)‖z‖^2.
(6) base.tex: the low-scale sum, the predictor telescoping identity, adaptive approximation, staggered pair-smallness (k_{t−7} = k_t^{A^{-7}}), the active-triple count (matched quadratic phases are killed by the exact marginal), and the active-cell reduction.
(7) counting.tex: the core powered estimate, including the amplitude exponent partial sums (−1 + θ'(1 + p_0), −2 + 2θ'(1 + p_0), −1 + θ'(1 + 3p_0); total 0, verified).
(8) completion.tex: the parameter order (q first, then α, then k_1). The coefficient of C_N is C_q Σ_t t·exp(−c_* k_t^θ), which can be made small.

Only skimmed: the internals of localization.tex (tag separation, usable Bessel spaces, catalog closure, the eq. 13 mismatch tests used for the far-band errors), most of linearization.tex (square energy for the linear side, eq. 17; top count; hereditary representatives), and the finite sparse counting lemma. Those carry the highest residual risk, and I could not verify them line by line at this effort level. I found no concrete failing step.
